title: A healing and a mercy
hookLine: We send down in the Qur'an what is a healing and a mercy (17:82)

lines: A CHIEF, STUNG BY A SCORPION.
HE STOOD UP, AS IF UNTIED.
cards: A desert camp, somewhere in Arabia. A small band of the Prophet's companions has stopped near a tribe that won't host them. That night the tribe's chief is stung by a scorpion, and nothing they try helps.
Someone comes over: does any of you know a cure? One companion says he does. He sits by the chief and recites the Fatiha over him, again and again, blowing lightly as he goes.
The hadith, in al-Bukhari, says the chief got up as if he'd been freed from a rope.

teach.b: Back in Medina, they told the Prophet ﷺ, and he asked the reciter: how did you know it was a ruqyah, a recitation for healing? He approved what they'd done. That story sits behind a word the Qur'an uses about itself.

teach.h: SHIFA': A HEALING AND A MERCY.
teach.b: Surah seventeen, verse eighty-two, in Pickthall's translation: "And We reveal of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for believers." The word for healing is shifa'.
Elsewhere the Qur'an calls itself a healing for what is in the breasts, the hearts, in surah ten, and a guidance and a healing in surah forty-one.

teach.h: FIRST, THE SICKNESS OF THE HEART.
teach.b: Notice which sickness these verses point to first. Commentators say it's in the heart: doubt, fear, grief, a restless mind. The book is a mercy for that.
Scholars also cite hadith like the scorpion story to hold that its recitation can be a means of healing for the body. And Islamic teaching doesn't set this against medicine.
A hadith in al-Bukhari says Allah has not sent down a disease without sending down a cure for it.

teach.h: MEDICINE IN ONE HAND, A VERSE IN THE OTHER.
teach.b: So shifa' comes in two hands at once: a doctor's prescription in one, a verse in the other. Neither has to cancel the other out. On a low day, the second hand is the one people sometimes forget they have.

how: In ruqyah, Muslims recite the Fatiha, the last two surahs and other verses over someone who is ill, alongside medical treatment; a hadith in al-Bukhari says Allah sent down no disease without its cure.

o: a mercy promised only in the next life
a cure that replaces seeing a doctor
healing, first of all for the heart

p: a healing and a mercy for believers
the Fatiha recited over a chief

s: Islamic teaching tells the sick to avoid medicine
a hadith says Allah sent down no disease without sending down its cure.
the Prophet approved the Fatiha recited over the stung chief
he asked how they knew it was a ruqyah.
the Qur'an calls itself a healing for what is in the hearts
surah ten speaks of a healing for what is in the breasts.

games.q: you're with the companions. a chief has been stung, nothing works, and they ask for a cure. what does the companion in the hadith do?
o: refuses, since they wouldn't host you.
sends for a doctor from Medina.
games.why: he recited the Fatiha, and the chief stood up as if freed from a rope. back in Medina, the Prophet approved.

practice: You don't have to be low right now; this is practice for the day you are. Bring to mind a short verse or line you know, the Fatiha or anything from this year that stayed with you, or simply the words a healing and a mercy.
Say it slowly three times, letting each word take a full breath, and notice whether anything in your chest loosens, even a little.

wordCard.voice: Shifa'. Healing. The Qur'an calls itself a healing and a mercy for believers, first for the heart, and recited, by the hadith, for the body too. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: healing. also a girl's name.

carryVoice: Your line: a healing. One line, held close, for the low days ahead. Until tomorrow.
